questions.stem: How common is myringotomy and grommet surgery in UK paediatric practice?
questions.answer: One of the commonest paediatric operations.

questions.stem: What does a myringotomy involve in paediatric ear surgery?
questions.answer: An incision in the tympanic membrane and suction of middle ear secretions.

questions.stem: What is often inserted alongside a myringotomy in children?
What are the main indications for myringotomy and grommets?
questions.answer: Recurrent otitis media and persistent middle ear effusion.

questions.stem: What position is used for a short myringotomy procedure?
questions.answer: Supine with the head turned to the side.

questions.stem: Is myringotomy usually done on one ear or both ears?
options: Only if the ear is discharging

questions.stem: Why must the child be kept still during myringotomy?
questions.answer: An operating microscope gives a magnified field.

questions.stem: Which age group mostly has myringotomy and grommets?
Which symptoms are common in children presenting for myringotomy and grommets?
Which congenital condition is notably common in children having myringotomy and grommets?
Which induction is common for myringotomy in young children with difficult venous access?
Which airway is usually used for myringotomy and grommets?
What is the usual maintenance for myringotomy and grommets?
questions.answer: Volatile in oxygen with air or nitrous oxide.

questions.stem: Which ventilation is the norm during myringotomy and grommets?
Which airway complication can occur during myringotomy?
How does postoperative pain after grommets tend to vary?
questions.answer: Unpredictable, from none to an inconsolable child.

questions.stem: What analgesia is usually enough after grommets?
options: Simple analgesia such as paracetamol and NSAIDs
